beliefs.practice: Create a single MongoClient (or equivalent driver client) at application startup and reuse it (singleton) across threads/requests rather than creating a new client per operation; close it only at process shutdown.
Read the cluster connection string/URI from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets store; never hard-code or commit credentials into repo or logs.
Require TLS/SSL for client connections and enable server certificate validation (e.g., include tls=true/ssl=true and ssl_cert_reqs in connection options).
Tune connection pool settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) in the MongoClient options appropriate to the app concurrency to avoid connection storms and to limit concurrent sockets to the cluster.
Set sensible driver timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS) to fail fast on unreachable cluster and avoid long-hanging requests in the orchestrator/agents.

Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient network and throttling errors (e.g., network errors, rate limit/429); make write operations idempotent or use retryable-writes where supported.
Prevent duplicate purchase orders by using an idempotency key and enforcing a unique index (or use upsert/update with unique key) on the purchase_orders collection instead of blind inserts.
Persist agent memory in a collection and enforce uniqueness on the deduplication key (e.g., (agent_id, event_hash)) via a unique index so concurrent orchestrations cannot create duplicate POs.

Choose a partition/shard key that collocates related reads/writes (e.g., product_id) so forecast queries and purchase order writes hit a single partition and avoid cross-partition queries and extra RU/IO cost.

Create indexes used by hot queries: index product_id and timestamp (or a compound index like {product_id:1, ts:-1}) for sales_velocity queries, and index supplier_id/lead_time fields used by supplier selection to make queries covered.

For vector search, create a vector index on the embedding field with the appropriate index type (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN), set the correct dimensionality, and tune search params (efSearch/efConstruction or equivalent) to trade quality for latency.
Avoid unbounded collection scans—always include indexed predicates in queries and avoid leading-wildcard regex or non-SARGable filters in the forecast and supplier queries.
Use explain()/query planner tools to verify that production queries use the intended indexes and to detect COLLSCANs; iterate indexes based on real explain output from the cluster.
Provision throughput appropriately (use autoscale if available) and monitor RU consumption, throttling (429), and request charge per query; tune indexes and queries to reduce RU cost.
Store secrets in Azure Key Vault or another secret manager instead of plain env vars for production; if env vars are used in dev, provide a .env.example placeholder and ensure .env is in .gitignore.

Follow least-privilege access: create a database user/credentials with only the read/write permissions needed for the sample_retail_09 database and collections rather than using a cluster admin key for the app.

Enforce document schema at either the application layer or via DB validation rules (JSON Schema validator) for sales_velocity, lead_times, and purchase_orders so agents can rely on fields being present and typed correctly.
Rely on the provider's backups/PITR capability for recovery and configure backup/retention appropriate to business needs; do not rely solely on ad-hoc dumps for production recovery.

Make seed and test scripts idempotent: use upserts, check for existence, and avoid destructive operations (drop) by default so running them against the live cluster does not unintentionally delete data.

Instrument and monitor the app: emit metrics for query latency, RU consumption per operation, connection pool usage, retries and failures, and set alerts for anomalous patterns (spikes in RUs, repeated throttling).
Use proper BSON/JSON types (numeric types for quantities, ISODate for timestamps) consistently in sales_velocity and purchase_orders so queries and indexing behave predictably.

If multiple writes must be atomic (e.g., write memory entry and purchase_order together), use multi-document transactions rather than separate writes only if the cluster and Mongo API version support transactions; otherwise design for idempotency and compensation logic.
Avoid skip-based pagination for large offsets; prefer range-based pagination (e.g., by timestamp or sort key) to keep queries fast and inexpensive.
Sanitize and validate any user/supplier input used in queries to avoid NoSQL-injection style attacks (e.g., prevent attacker-supplied objects that become query operators).

When combining vector similarity with metadata filters, push the metadata filters into the vector search API (or use a vector+filter operator) so the vector index can prune candidates and avoid expensive post-filtering.
